title: Message Pop
blurb: A short rising pop, the universal shape of a new message arriving. It deliberately isn't any one app's chime, and that vagueness is the useful part: it reads unmistakably as "you've got a text" without borrowing a trademarked sound. Notification designers converge on this shape because a quick upward pitch bend reads as positive and non-urgent, unlike an alarm's flat repetition. Editors drop it over on-screen texts, streamers wire it to chat alerts, and pranksters play it near people mid-conversation just for the reflexive phone check.
origin: Original synthesis in the style of generic messaging-app pops.
